key_insight: The paper replaces post hoc semi-local rescaling with elliptic-equation-defined transformed coordinates and velocities, enabling a density-aware wall coordinate for compressible turbulence.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more principled inner-layer scaling tool for high-speed wall-bounded flows with heat transfer, improving profile collapse and near-wall interpretation across different thermal conditions.
method: Define a semi-local wall coordinate from local density and viscosity.
Solve a Helmholtz-type elliptic equation for a bounded density-induced coordinate correction.
Use projection equations to obtain the transformed coordinate Y+ and transformed velocity U+ from mean velocity, density, viscosity, wall distance, and wall normals.
evidence_signal: A single calibrated set of wall-layer constants from two cooled flat plates was tested on boundary layers and channel flows, with improved inner and buffer-layer placement reported especially for cooled high-speed boundary layers.
watch_item: The approach depends on calibrated wall-layer constants and accurate mean property fields; performance may be sensitive to flow configuration and how density is defined in channel half-domains.
paper_title: Semi-local transformation for compressible wall turbulence via elliptic equations
